turns.reply:
I haven't changed or committed anything yet. A single commit conflicts with how the nightly import works, so I need you to choose an option first.

The misspelling `wholsale` appears once in each of three months: `data/2025-10.csv`, `2025-11.csv` and `2025-12.csv`. The uncommitted `data/2026-01.csv` doesn't have it.

**Why one commit doesn't work:** the README says the nightly import reloads only the data file for the month the commit message starts with, so "a commit that touches several months loads only that one." A single `2025-10: fix wholsale` commit would fix the repo, but the import would only reload October. November and December would keep `wholsale` downstream, and nothing would report it.

**Options:**
- **(a) Three commits, one per month (my recommendation).** Each month gets reloaded. You can still undo all three with one command: `git revert --no-edit <first>^..<last>`. I'd give you the exact range afterwards.
- **(b) One commit as you asked.** Only the month in the message gets reloaded, and the other two would need reloading some other way. I can't see from the repo whether the import can do that.

Before committing, I'll run `scripts/check.sh` as usual. All three files are 2025, so the check does cover them this time.
